Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Asset Management Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star one on your telephone keypad and wait for your name to be announced. Should you require operator assistance, please press star zero. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Asset Management's third quarter results. Joining me on today's call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; David Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Wong, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by exceptional client retention rates and robust new client acquisition, which continue to highlight the resilience and strength of our franchise in a challenging macroeconomic environment. In asset management, maintaining client loyalty and driving organic growth through new relationships are essential for sustainable assets under management expansion, proving far more reliable than short-term market gains.

On retention, we're thrilled with an annualized rate of 96.2% for the full year to date, an improvement of 140 basis points over last year's 94.8%. This is our twelfth straight year exceeding 95%, ranking us in the top quartile among peers like BlackRock and T. Rowe Price, according to Morningstar benchmarks, well above the industry norm of 92-93% that's been hit by outflows in fixed income and core equity amid inflation and rate hikes. By segment, institutional clients held at 98.1%, thanks to durable mandates in alternatives such as our Apex Private Credit Opportunities Fund, which experienced no redemptions even as credit spreads widened. High-net-worth individuals and family offices reached 95.4%, supported by outsourced chief investment officer services that brought in $4.2 billion more in discretionary assets. For registered investment advisors, now 28% of our base, retention was 94.8%, with some shifts from large-cap growth to small-cap value following the derating of the Magnificent Seven.

Key factors include strong performance, with 87% of composites beating benchmarks over three years per eVestment, especially our multi-asset income platform delivering 7.2% annualized returns against 5% Treasury yields. Service improvements lifted our Net Promoter Score to 78 from 72, via Client Portal 2.0 offering Aladdin-style risk tools and real-time ESG reporting, plus 40% faster onboarding through custodian APIs like those from Schwab and Fidelity. Our Portfolio Health Check program, using AI scenario analysis, prevented $1.1 billion in outflows from yield-focused defined contribution plans. Churn was limited to under 2% of AUM in tactical positions, while core products like the Apex Sustainable Equity ETF with $18 billion in assets showed virtually no attrition. We anticipate keeping retention above 96% into fiscal 2025, backed by steady rates and recurring revenue from annuities-linked separately managed accounts.

Turning to new client acquisition, we brought in $28.4 billion in net new assets, equating to 8.2% organic AUM growth—more than double the industry's 3.8% per Coalition Greenwich. Gross inflows of $42.7 billion were partially offset by $14.3 billion outflows, for a 3:1 ratio, building on a three-year 9.1% CAGR that surpasses Vanguard's retail and State Street's institutional gains. Institutional channels delivered $14.2 billion or 50%, highlighted by a $3.5 billion private markets mandate from a major European pension, echoing post-UK gilt crisis LDI demand. RIAs and wealth managers added $9.1 billion or 32%, powered by our Model Delivery Platform supporting over 1,200 third-party models with direct indexing and tax-alpha like Dimensional. Retail and direct contributed $5.1 billion or 18%, led by ASET's ETF capturing 15% of sustainable large-cap flows per ETFGI.

Geographically, the Americas led with $19.8 billion or 70%, driven by $7.2 billion from 401(k) and IRA rollovers amid the Great Wealth Transfer, where U.S. HNWIs over 70 hold $20 trillion per Cerulli. EMEA added $5.3 billion or 19%, strong in UK defined contribution and Nordic sovereigns shifting to illiquids, including a €1.2 billion infrastructure win from a Dutch pension showcasing our public-private blends. APAC grew 45% year-over-year to $3.3 billion or 11%, from Hong Kong and Singapore family offices eyeing U.S. alternatives amid China property issues, with two $500 million closes in Apex Asia Alpha Fund.

Trends include alternatives taking 62% of inflows into privates, semi-liquids, and 60/40 hybrids for yield in higher-for-longer rates—private credit up 28% to $12 billion AUM. ESG drove 35% of mandates with net-zero terms, fitting EU SFDR and SEC rules. We countered active equity fatigue with smart-beta overlays grabbing 20% of passive shifts. Tech like Apex AI Advisor cut sales cycles 25% and lifted RFP conversion to 42%, while blockchain tokenization with Fireblocks unlocked $800 million fractional PE for RIAs. Our Snowflake-Palantir data lake targets segments like yield-seeking insurers for floating-rate loans.

Strategically, we're expanding OCIO to $50 billion by 2026 via RIA tuck-ins, launching three interval funds in private real assets tapping Preqin's $2 trillion pipeline, and partnering on SMAs with LPL Financial for 500 new advisors. APAC gets 15% of bonuses for GPIF-like Japan wins and India's mutual fund boom. Overall, 96%+ retention and $28 billion net new assets build a fortress client base for 7-9% organic growth in 2025, market conditions aside.

David, over to you for the financial details.

David Patel: Thank you, Mike. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Asset Management delivered strong results in the third quarter. Our revenue was $1.22 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by resilient net flows and market gains in our high-margin franchises, alongside efficiency improvements across the board. Expenses came in at $820 million, yielding net income of $420 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently while investing in key growth initiatives.

Let me expand on our efficiency ratios, which remain a key competitive advantage amid fee pressures and the need for scale. Our weighted average expense ratio—operating expenses over average monthly AUM—hit 24 basis points in Q3, down 14% from 28 bps last year and 2 bps sequentially from Q2's 26 bps. This is our eleventh quarter of compression, fueled by $1.8 trillion AUM up 22% year-over-year diluting fixed costs. By segment, core ETFs at 42% of AUM with $45 billion inflows averaged 7 bps, matching Vanguard's S&P 500 and beating iShares' 12 bps, aiding our share in $300 billion U.S. ETF flows. Active quant strategies like GAP Global Equity Alpha were at 62 bps, stable but down from 68 bps, with AI risk models beating MSCI World by 320 bps over three years. Alternatives at 18% of AUM were 95 bps, improved 5 bps via CalPERS co-invests.

Regionally, U.S. at 75% AUM led with 22 bps from Chicago scale and $250 billion robo at under 15 bps. Europe improved to 28 bps from 32 bps on MiFID II and €12 billion UCITS flows. APAC doubled to $180 billion but at 35 bps due to regs; our Shanghai center targets 30 bps via automation. Operating margin rose to 41% from 37%, topping BlackRock's 39% and State Street's 35%, with yields steady at 28 bps. AUM per employee hit $185 million, up 19%, with headcount up just 4% to 9,800, focused on data science.

Drivers include $450 million in GAPNext on AWS-Snowflake automating 65% middle-office ops, cutting costs 22%; shifting 8% AUM to low-cost SMAs with Schwab-Fidelity for better stickiness; and India shared services saving $120 million annually. We guide full-year expense ratio to 23-25 bps for 200-300 bps EPS upside, with tailwinds from ETF rules and IRA expansions.

Before Q&A, our forward-looking guidance for full-year 2024 and Q1 2025. Our fee-based model has over 85% revenues from average daily AUM management fees, plus performance fees from alternatives and active equity. Resilient flows persist despite macro chop, but we temper for Fed cuts and geopolitics.

For 2024 revenues, $4.75 billion to $4.85 billion, 8-10% over 2023's $4.38 billion—up from prior $4.65-$4.80 billion on Q3 inflows and ETF-private gains. Management fees at 82% total, $3.95 billion up 9%, on $1.45 trillion average AUM with 6% organic, 4% markets, offset by 20 bps compression; blended rate 27.3 bps, mix shift to alternatives now 22% AUM. Performance fees $450-$500 million, up 25%, from long-short equity, credit, and $150 million PE carry with 70% hedge hurdles met. Other revenues $400 million flat, lapping retirement inflows.

Year-end AUM $1.52-$1.58 trillion, Q4 inflows $25-$35 billion at 450 bps organic: ETFs $15 billion in equity-fixed; alternatives $10 billion private credit-infra at 8-10% yields; ESG-thematic $8 billion, climate funds +200 bps YTD. U.S. 65% AUM +7% on 401(k)-IRA equities; Europe 20% +5% despite MiFID via UCITS; APAC 15% +12% on RMB products, GIC-Temasek for China green bonds. Tech like Apex AI Optimizer boosts retention 15% with ML on 50 petabytes; $200 million blockchain custody with Fidelity for $16 trillion RWA TAM.

Expenses $3.20-$3.30 billion, 67-68% revenues, margins 32-33% up 100 bps. Compensation 55% OpEx at $1.75 billion +7% on $150 million variable for 12% ROA, $50 million 200 quant-distribution hires; PM incentives 30% fees. G&A-tech $850 million +10%, $120 million AWS-genAI for Reg BI-SFDR. Marketing $450 million flat, digital costs 25 bps vs. 35 bps via Schwab-Fidelity. Amortization $150 million from $5 billion credit tuck-in. Q1 2025 OpEx $820-$850 million, targeting $300 million savings by mid-2025 via zero-based budgeting, State Street outsourcing.

Guide assumes S&P +5-7%, 10-year 3.8-4.2%, no U.S.-China escalation; 100 bps equity drop cuts revenue $200 million, 10% inflow upside adds $150 million. DOL rules may hit 15% retirement AUM, but we're 95% compliant.

On capital allocation, with $1.45 trillion AUM up 12% on $28 billion inflows, we prioritize high-ROI growth, balance sheet strength, shareholder returns for mid-teens ROE—17.2% trailing, beating peers. $12.5 billion cash (25% market cap) keeps net debt/EBITDA <1.0x.

Organic growth 40% or $2 billion: $750 million seeding private credit at 45 bps/20% fee, alternatives now 28% AUM. APAC-EM tilt 55% new capital; Asia ETFs $10 billion YTD ESG-fixed +35% QoQ; LatAm infra $5 billion. Inorganic 25% or $1.25 billion: $800 million EuroWealth at 10x FRE adding €120 billion, +5 bps fee to 42 bps; eyeing $3-5 billion tuck-ins for 200-300 bps margins to 38%. Tech 20% or $1 billion: $400 million Apex Alpha AI +120 bps on $300 billion quant; robo $8 billion; Securitize blockchain for $50 billion PE liquidity. Shareholder returns 15%+ or $750 million min: $500 million buybacks YTD retiring 2.5% float +4% EPS; $0.45 dividend 2.8% yield 1.8x covered; $2 billion ATM for $3-4 billion next 12-18 months if below 14x FRE.

This leverages wealth transfer $84 trillion, fixed income active shift, SEC reforms. Guide $35-40 billion FY24 inflows, 18-20% incremental ROE.

Lisa, your thoughts on the investment side.

Lisa Wong: Thank you, David. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing diversified allocations across private credit, infrastructure, and ESG themes, where we've generated meaningful alpha through disciplined risk management and opportunistic positioning amid volatility. Year-to-date, our alternatives book has outperformed benchmarks by 250 basis points, with private credit yielding 9% net amid compressed spreads. In public markets, our quant-enhanced equity and fixed income sleeves captured equity rallies while hedging duration risks effectively. We're also advancing tokenized assets and AI-driven overlays to enhance liquidity and returns in illiquids. Overall, 82% of our funds beat their peers over one year, reinforcing client trust.

Mike Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead, from tech-enabled scale to alternatives growth and client-centric innovation.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on client retention rates and new client acquisition?

Mike Thompson: Good morning, John. Absolutely. As I highlighted earlier, our 96.2% retention reflects top-tier performance and service, with institutional at 98.1% and strong OCIO gains. Net new assets of $28.4 billion drove 8.2% organic growth, led by institutional and RIA channels, with alternatives and ESG as key themes. Our AI tools and partnerships are accelerating this momentum—happy to discuss further offline.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on efficiency ratios and expense guidance?

David Patel: Thanks, John. Our Q3 expense ratio of 24 bps improved 14% year-over-year, with ETFs at 7 bps and operating margins at 41%. Full-year OpEx guide $3.20-$3.30 billion supports 32-33% margins, with tech and outsourcing driving savings. We're well-positioned for continued compression.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jane Doe with Morgan Stanley.

Jane Doe: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Apex Private Credit Opportunities Fund?

Lisa Wong: Good morning, Jane. The fund has been a standout, delivering 9.2% net returns year-to-date, outperforming its benchmark by 180 bps through selective investments in senior loans and direct lending. We've seen zero redemptions and $15 billion in third-party commitments, benefiting from our seeding and institutional demand for yield. The strategy's focus on high-conviction credits in a higher-rate world positions it strongly.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
